name: Bam
description: Bam (also widely known as Pluck) is a cutthroat trick-taking game primarily for three players, though four-player partnerships exist. Its defining feature is the 'Plucking' mechanic: after the first hand, players who met their trick quotas get to steal the best cards from those who failed, creating a slippery slope where the rich get richer and the poor struggle to recover. It uses a specialized 51-card deck (removing small 2s) and features asymmetric trick targets for the dealer and opponents.

content.text: Bam (also widely known as Pluck) is a cutthroat trick-taking game primarily for three players, though four-player partnerships exist. Its defining feature is the 'Plucking' mechanic: after the first hand, players who met their trick quotas get to steal the best cards from those who failed, creating a slippery slope where the rich get richer and the poor struggle to recover. It uses a specialized 51-card deck (removing small 2s) and features asymmetric trick targets for the dealer and opponents.
Likely evolved from Whist or Spades variations in the American Midwest, incorporating the 'card exchange' penalty found in games like President (Scum) but applied to a trick-taking structure.
51 Cards: remove 2♦, 2♥, 2♠. Keep 2♣. Add 2 distinct Jokers (Big and Little).
Deal all cards. Each player receives 17 cards. (4-player version deals 13 cards).

items.text: Four Player Partnership: Standard 52 cards (no Jokers, or Jokers replace low cards). Teams must make a bid. Plucking involves passing cards between partners.
Dropsy: A variation where the plucking rules are stricter; players must drop ('give') their cards before seeing what they get back.
